item.title: Minimap 1.0 Add-On
item.creator: ThunderAy
item.description:
A Minimap Add-On built to run smooth in ANY world, not slow your game down!
- 5 resolution levels and 3 zoom levels: zoom out for better view, raise resolution for better details.
- One-tap performance presets. We recommend starting low and raising only if your device stays smooth.
- Two modes: steady offhand Minimap, or floating with no offhand requirement.
- Waypoints

faqEntries.heading: Which settings should I use?
faqEntries.content:
Start low. We recommend the lower Map Resolution options and raising them one step at a time, only while the game still feels smooth. 16x16 is the default and the lightest. 64x64 is the most demanding and suits higher-end devices.

The quickest route is Presets > Low, which sets everything in one tap. The game also warns you when a setting may cause problems on low-end devices.

faqEntries.heading: The minimap is slowing my game down. What should I change?
faqEntries.content:
Lower your Map Resolution first, it has by far the biggest impact. Then apply the Low preset. Zoom Level costs nothing, so you can zoom out freely without affecting performance.
If you are the world owner, lower the Map Resolution Limit in Host Settings so the cap applies to everyone in the world.

faqEntries.heading: Does the minimap use my offhand slot?
faqEntries.content: We have two options. It uses the offhand by default. If you would rather keep the slot free at all times, turn on Allow Offhand to switch to the floating minimap. That mode is marked Experimental.

faqEntries.heading: How do I create a waypoint, and how many can I have?
faqEntries.content: Sneak and use the Waypoint Controller to drop one where you stand, or open it and choose Create. Give each waypoint a name, color, icon and visibility. Choose Directions on any waypoint and the minimap shows you the way, the distance, and tells you when you have arrived.

faqEntries.heading: Why can I not teleport to my waypoint?
faqEntries.content:
Teleporting is off by default. A world owner has to turn on Enable Teleportation in Host Settings.
Once it is on, teleporting costs XP unless Free Warps is enabled, has a cooldown, takes a couple of seconds to charge, and cannot cross dimensions. World owners can adjust all of those.

faqEntries.heading: Does this work in my existing world, the Nether and the End?
faqEntries.content:
Yes to all three. Add the pack to any world, new or existing.
Waypoints record their dimension so you can tell them apart, and directions to a waypoint in another dimension tell you which portal to enter.

howToEntries.heading: Open your Minimap settings
howToEntries.content:
Three ways, whichever suits you:

- Use the Minimap Settings item.
- Read the Guide Book that comes with the pack.
- Type the command /lpsm_minimap:minimap.

World owners get an extra menu, Host Settings, with options that apply to everyone.
On a Realm you must set your permission to Operator in the Realm's member settings to
open it.

howToEntries.heading: Choose your Map Resolution (do this first)
howToEntries.content:
Minimap Settings > Performance > Map Resolution. This is the map's size in pixels:

16x16 · 24x24 · 32x32 · 48x48 · 64x64

It starts at 16x16. Higher is sharper, lower is easier on your device.

We recommend leaving it low and raising it one step at a time. Play for a minute after
each step, and stop as soon as the game stops feeling smooth. Phones, tablets and older
consoles should expect to stay at the lower end. The game shows a warning when you pick a setting that may cause problems on low-end devices.

howToEntries.heading: Use a performance preset instead
howToEntries.content:
Minimap Settings > Presets. Three built-in presets, Low, Medium and High, set everything for you in one tap. Low is the safe starting point on any device.

You can also save your own setup as a custom preset and re-apply it later.

howToEntries.heading: Set your Zoom Level
howToEntries.content:
Minimap Settings > Zoom Level.

Close — see detail nearby (default)
Medium — a balanced view
Far — see more terrain

Zoom and resolution do different jobs. Zoom out to see more of the world. Raise the
resolution to see it in more detail. Zoom costs you nothing in performance; resolution does.

howToEntries.heading: Place the minimap where you want it
howToEntries.content:
Minimap Settings > Appearance.

Map Position — Map Position — Top Right (default), Top Left, Bottom Left, Bottom Right, Center, or Custom with the horizontal and vertical offset sliders

Minimap Size — six steps from smallest to largest, default is the middle

Map Shape — Square (default) or Rounded

Rotate Minimap — turn it on to make the map turn with you like a compass. Off keeps
the map fixed north-up

Show Compass — the N/E/S/W markers, on by default

Border Color — any of the 16 standard colors

howToEntries.heading: Choose your minimap mode
howToEntries.content:
Minimap Settings > Allow Offhand.

Off (default) — the steady minimap. It uses your offhand slot, stays locked in place on
screen, and is the smoother of the two.

On — the floating minimap. It leaves your offhand slot free. This mode is marked as Experimental: it can jitter while you move.
